# prompts that worked

## i2v:

single image in image_0

```
You are a helpful assistant specialized in text-to-video generation.

From image_0 the woman performs a high-energy cheerleader dance routine. She executes a high jump, then a cartwheel across the stage. Her ponytail bounces with the movement. She does a high kick toward the front of the stage, followed by the splits at the back of the stage, clapping her hands above her head once. Fast-paced, highly energetic. Smooth, fluid motion. She stays on the theatre stage the entire time.
```

```
You are a helpful assistant specialized in text-to-video generation.

From image_0 cinematic long shot, smooth continuous orbiting camera rotating steadily around the subjects. The camera circles the scene in a fluid 360-degree arc. Three nymphs playfully interact with a satyr, gathered around a rocky pool at a cascading waterfall. 19th-century French academic oil painting style, William-Adolphe Bouguereau aesthetic, lush forest background, soft dappled sunlight, masterpiece, highly detailed, realistic lighting, steady camera motion, high temporal consistency, no morphing, 5-second continuous shot.
```

```
You are a helpful assistant specialized in image-to-video generation.

A 5-second cinematic video clip. From image_0, use the dimly lit, narrow theatre backstage corridor with exposed brick walls, overhead pipes, and warm amber fluorescent lights as the environment. From image_1, take the two women and the man and add them to the corridor. The two women are running ahead of the man, pulling him by his arms toward the end of the corridor. They keep looking back excitedly toward the camera as they pull him forward. The camera follows behind at the same pace as them, capturing their dynamic movement down the hallway. Realistic motion, cinematic lighting, high quality.
```

try all sorts of combinations it is interesting what works and what doesnt. This model can even swap people out and remove them but I found it wont swap people at a distance so there is some limit to it. I really only used it for its i2v usefulness and structure for upscaling after with LTX.

Use from image0, from image1, from image2 for the reference names - that's how they were trained

"from image0" is what was most common (from)
replace the X with the person "from image0" ... It'll work with other wordings, but that's how they trained it

widgets_values:
# If using video and ref images

To LOCK first initial image all three ref must be plugged with the same initial image

source_video
reference_video
reference_image_0 

All must have the same image for i2v locking the first frame
total steps will be split between the two samplers e.g. "a/2" means 6 steps will be 3 high and 3 low. (6 steps was default)

Bernini is 480p or 720p max (theoretically)

I tried 1920 but couldnt get it going on 3060. trying 1440 long edge finished in 22 mins and was pretty good. trying 1600 but it failed on the last step and never finished.

16fps because WAN 2.2 though people set it to 24fps that will only work on v2v. it will likely do fast motion at 24fps for i2v. Use RIFe interpolation to get from 16fps native WAN to 24fps.

FPS INTERPOLATION:

Set it to Rife x3 with "every nth" node set to 2 will go 16fps > 48fps > 24fps output.

I am currently preferring 30fps for results here with Bernini it just seems slightly better to me for sideways movements so I am only using it set to x2 rife interpolate and saving out at 32 fps.

# markdkberry.com

Updated: 27th June 2026

I really like Bernini for structure work as the prompts are Wan focused and its faster than WAN models for i2v (but slow for v2v so be warned). I also pretty sure it is 480p limit but the -R version may be different. I havent downloaded them to test, but see notes below on Bytedance rug pulling the one I was using and what to use instead. I havent confirmed how well they work but Kijai thinks they are as good.

## MODELS

*(NOTE: ComfyUI has signalled that GGUFs are going to become a thing of the past in ComfyUI support if possible use int8 models (update comfyui) but failing that fp8)*


https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Bernini-R/blob/main/diffusion_models/wan2.2_bernini_r_high_noise_int8_convrot.safetensors

https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Bernini-R/blob/main/diffusion_models/wan2.2_bernini_r_low_noise_int8_convrot.safetensors


---

## SAMPLER OPTIONS

You can setup the usual dual Wan 2.2 sampler method as has been done here. There is also the other single sampler approach workflow that uses **WanMOEKsampler**

## MODELS

I was using GGUFs originally but have switched to int8 models now to take advantage of Comfyui dynamic memory management. this requires updates from early July 2026.

[https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Bernini-R/blob/main/diffusion_models/wan2.2_bernini_r_high_noise_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Bernini-R/blob/main/diffusion_models/wan2.2_bernini_r_high_noise_int8_convrot.safetensors)

[https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Bernini-R/blob/main/diffusion_models/wan2.2_bernini_r_low_noise_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Bernini-R/blob/main/diffusion_models/wan2.2_bernini_r_low_noise_int8_convrot.safetensors)

the above runs on 3060 RTX with 32 gb system ram but the mode nodes that get loaded in the more problems it can create so be aware of the int8 setup requirements. you might be better with fp8 or learning more about int8 vrs custom nodes, before use. 



---

## SPEED TESTS & WHY I LIKE BERNINI:

I like it for structure and sending that at 480p to LTX for upscaling and detailing.

- i2v 480p this workflow is done in about 7 mins on my machine for 81 frames (16fps). I like the prompt, I like the speed, 16fp then interpolates to 24fps and its 5 seconds long. Ideal for building clips for music videos, and I enjoyed using this for making my recent one.

- with video editing it is slow. 832 on long edge (2.39:1) was done in 10 minutes 81 frames (v2v, i2v is faster) once I added in sage attn and chunk. 241 frames was ridiculously long as I think it loses the plot others are using context windows but I havent bothered, but 161 frames was done under 20 mins.
